dialogues.speaker: Lyubava
dialogues.text: Heh, all grown up and still like this... What a fool.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you calling a fool?

dialogues.speaker: Lyubava
dialogues.text: Who else? My Ignasha, that blockhead! All day long, all he thinks about is making money, and he can't even say one sweet thing to me. Tell me, what kind of husband is that?

dialogues.speaker: Lyubava
dialogues.text: I've told him many times not to take those night shifts, but he just won't listen. Keeps saying the night shift pays better! How much better can it be? Not even enough to cover the doctor's bill.

dialogues.speaker: Lyubava
dialogues.text: Hmph. If he really does end up sick one day, I'm going to sit by his bed and laugh at him every single day. And I'll feed him his most hated borscht, too. Then we'll see if he still dares not to listen to me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if he's saving money for you?

dialogues.speaker: Lyubava
dialogues.text: I still wouldn't agree with it! With the little he's saved, how is he supposed to buy a house in Snezhnograd? He didn't even think to include money for renovations and furniture. Honestly, he's such an idiot!

dialogues.speaker: Lyubava
dialogues.text: But... I'll let you in on a secret. I've actually been saving up some money myself. Once he buys the house and realizes he's short, I'm going to let him stew for a few days first. Make him panic!

dialogues.speaker: Lyubava
dialogues.text: Then, when he's just about to cry, I'll slap the money down right in front of him! That'll teach him a proper lesson, and show him who really has the final say in this family!
